title: The Map Beneath the Sunflowers
subtitle: A Copper Tree story and colouring adventure

pages.heading: A glint in the soil
pages.text: Saturday was garden day in Copper Tree. Nia watered the sunflowers. Eli collected empty pots. Amara, Kofi and Tayo helped Mrs Bennett tidy the path. Zuri was looking for beetles when something flashed beneath a leaf. “Treasure!” she cried. Mrs Bennett helped her lift a little tin from the loose soil. Its lid was tightly shut. It rattled. Definitely treasure.
pages.activity: Draw a garden with something tiny Zuri might discover beneath a leaf.
pages.art_brief: Zuri kneeling beside sunflower bed, beaded braids and yellow jacket, Mrs Bennett helping lift a small rectangular tin. Other five friends doing garden tasks, spacious simple composition.

pages.heading: A message from before
pages.text: Inside were a photograph, a folded map and a note. “For whoever finds this: there is still one thing we never finished.” The photograph showed three children beside the old garden shed. On the map, a dotted line joined a bell, a book and a star. “A spaceship landing place,” whispered Tayo. “My mystery,” said Zuri, holding it close.
pages.activity: Draw and decorate a treasure tin of your own. Add the things you would put inside.
pages.art_brief: Open rectangular tin with folded map, photograph of three children by shed, blank note; six curious faces around it. Keep symbols bell, book, star large and clear, no generated text.

pages.heading: The bell at the market
pages.text: Mrs Bennett agreed to walk with them. At Saturday Market, Zuri spotted a stallholder’s bell. “First clue!” Kofi pointed to the photograph. “There’s something behind—” “Later!” said Zuri. She asked about the bell. The stallholder shook his head. “Bought it last Tuesday.” Zuri’s shoulders dropped. The map looked much older than that.
pages.activity: Design a market stall selling three things you would love to find.
pages.art_brief: Zuri and Kofi at market stall with handbell, Mrs Bennett and other friends nearby. Clear disappointed and tentative expressions. Wide spaces on stall for reader drawings.

pages.heading: A mystery with room
pages.text: They sat on a bench. Kofi had stopped pointing. Zuri looked at the map, then at her friends. “I didn’t let you finish,” she said. “Sorry. Will you show me?” Kofi smiled and turned the photograph round. Behind the children was a bell on the shed wall. “Our first clue was back in the garden!”
pages.activity: Draw how Zuri feels before and after asking Kofi for help. What could her face show?
pages.art_brief: Zuri offering photograph to Kofi on bench, friends listening with Mrs Bennett. Photograph shows bell beside shed door. Leave two large face frames for emotional drawing separately in layout.

pages.heading: The book by the bell
pages.text: Back at the garden, Nia found the bell beneath a climbing plant. Beside it, Amara spotted a painted book. “It matches the map!” Mrs Bennett laughed. “I painted that! We wanted a story corner here.” Zuri held out the photograph for her to see. Mrs Bennett peered closely. “Goodness! That’s me with my friends!”
pages.activity: Draw climbing leaves around a painted symbol for your favourite activity.
pages.art_brief: Garden shed outside, Nia gently parting leaves to reveal old bell, Amara pointing at simple open-book symbol painted on wall; Mrs Bennett recognising photograph. Shed door stays closed.

pages.heading: The unfinished corner
pages.text: “Why didn’t you finish?” asked Eli. “The roof leaked,” said Mrs Bennett. “We packed our things into that tin to keep them dry. Then my family moved. The tin vanished during a garden tidy-up.” She looked at the weeds. “The roof was repaired later. The story corner was forgotten.” “Until now,” said Nia.
pages.activity: Draw the story corner as you imagine it. Include somewhere comfortable to sit.
pages.art_brief: Mrs Bennett and children standing outside ordinary weathered shed and overgrown adjacent sitting corner, holding tin. Open generous design area for child’s imagined seating; no dangerous roof work.

pages.heading: Follow the little star
pages.text: Eli studied the map. “The star is beside the door.” They found a faded star on a loose wooden sign, tucked behind a flowerpot. Underneath were the words STORY CORNER. Tayo grinned. “So the treasure is a place!” Zuri laid the map where everyone could see it. “What could we make here together?”
pages.activity: Make a sign for a place you would share with friends. Add your own symbol.
pages.art_brief: Eli discovering small sign behind pot beside closed shed, star prominent; Zuri spreading map on garden table; Tayo delighted. Show sign artwork blank for typeset words or reader design.

pages.heading: Six different ideas
pages.text: Amara wanted a mural. Kofi wanted a discovery shelf. Nia wanted flowers by the door. Eli suggested a games basket. Tayo asked for somewhere to look at the sky. Zuri wanted a big map. “And space for new friends,” she added. Mrs Bennett nodded. “Let’s ask the garden committee. A shared place needs a shared plan.”
pages.activity: Draw one thing you would add to the friends’ shared place. Where would it fit?
pages.art_brief: Six children around garden table each contributing a simple picture plan, Mrs Bennett listening. Keep room for seventh idea, cheerful varied poses, avoid crowded map detail.

pages.heading: Many helping hands
pages.text: The committee said yes. Adults checked the shed and fixed its stiff door. Uncle Deji put up shelves. The children washed pots, sorted books and painted with Mrs Bennett. When Zuri tried to carry too many cushions, Eli caught the tumbling one. “Expedition rescued,” he announced. Zuri laughed. “Thank you, Chief Cushion Catcher.”
pages.activity: Design three cushions with different patterns. Invent a funny helper title for yourself.
pages.art_brief: Safe garden work day, adults installing shelf, children sorting books washing pots and painting low wall. Eli catching one cushion falling from Zuri’s stack, playful expressions. No children using power tools.

pages.heading: The Lookout
pages.text: A week later, six mismatched seats waited inside. Amara’s mural curled around Kofi’s discovery shelf. Nia’s flowers stood outside. The games basket sat below a map with plenty of blank space. “We need a name,” said Tayo. “We look out for discoveries,” said Zuri. “And each other,” added Nia. “The Lookout!” they shouted.
pages.activity: Design a tiny mural for the Lookout. Leave space for another person to add something.
pages.art_brief: Finished shed interior with six mismatched seats, books, games basket, shelf, large partly blank map, bright uncluttered mural. Six friends delighted. Flowers visible outside open door.

pages.heading: Everyone brings something
pages.text: At the opening, neighbours brought books, bunting and a plate of warm buns. Grandad Leon challenged Eli to a game. Mrs Bennett rang the old bell with its new rope. Zuri showed everyone the photograph. “We found their unfinished idea,” she said. “Then everyone helped it grow.” Tayo checked the sky. “Still room for a spaceship.”
pages.activity: Draw yourself at the celebration. What would you bring to share?
pages.art_brief: Welcoming garden celebration outside shed, diverse neighbours, six children, Mrs Bennett ringing bell with new rope, Grandad Leon playing simple board game with Eli. Large open foreground space for reader portrait.

pages.heading: For whoever comes next
pages.text: The tin became the first treasure on the discovery shelf. Together, the friends wrote a new message: “There is room for your ideas here.” Zuri tucked it inside and left the lid open. Outside, the sunflowers nodded over the path. “What shall we discover next?” she asked. This time, she waited to hear everybody’s answer.
pages.activity: Draw your next adventure. Who comes with you, and what might you discover?
pages.art_brief: Close view of open tin on discovery shelf, note blank for typesetting, photograph alongside; six friends in doorway facing welcoming garden, sunflowers outside. End with open space for next-adventure drawing.
